disagreements.topic: Net buyback accretion and FY28 EPS
disagreements.positions: Agents 1 and 3 use about 3.5%/yr net share reduction (agent 1 haircuts for funding from SBC-burdened FCF less dividends); agents 2, 4 and 5 use about 4%. FY28 EPS: agent 3 $25.0, agents 2/4/5 $25.5, agent 1 $25.6.
disagreements.resolution: Accretion is higher than any agent (or my round-1 file) assumed. The FY26 10-K equity statement shows only 2.6M shares issued under employee plans net of tax withholding against 13.4M repurchased, so the count fell 279.1M -> 268.4M (-3.8%) while buying at an average of about $409. Net issuance is about 1%/yr, not the 2.5-3% I used in round 1. At about $270, $5-6B a year buys 7-8% gross, about 5-6% net. Funding is not binding: SBC is non-cash, so the relevant pool is OCF less capex (about $7.3B normalized plus about $0.7B of remaining OBBBA tax benefit) less a dividend of about $1.5B, which leaves about $6.5B. Cash and investments are $7.2B against $7.7B of debt, and $7.9B of authorization remains. Agent 1's haircut counts SBC twice. FY28 EPS of about $25.8 is better supported than $25.0-25.5.
disagreements.evidence: Intuit FY26 10-K: stockholders' equity statement (issuance under employee plans 2,621K shares; repurchases 13,366K for $5,463M; shares 279,129K -> 268,384K); liquidity table (cash and investments $7.2B, debt principal $7.72B, $1.25B due FY27); Note 11 ($7.9B authorization). 8-K of 2026-03-16 (accelerated repurchases).

disagreements.topic: Size of the left tail after round 1
disagreements.positions: Everyone lowered their thesis break and bear prices after the HRB 6.6x finding. Agent 5 went furthest (a 20% Chegg-type branch, P(>=214)=0.71, bear $160); agent 1 kept a 33% bear weight at $185; agents 2-4 have 25-28% at $165-175.
disagreements.resolution: Round 2 turned up no new negative fundamental fact. The new evidence is mildly positive: insider 10b5-1 plans terminated, repurchases accelerated, and QBO list prices up about 22-24% on Plus/Advanced. So the further drop in the center of the ladder (P(>=268) 0.574 -> 0.555) is the agents absorbing my round-1 tail finding, not independent confirmation. I keep the fatter left tail (the round-2 mean, about 0.74 at 214) and give back about a point in the middle for the buyback correction.
disagreements.evidence: Round-2 revisions lists; 8-K 2026-03-16; Intuit QuickBooks pricing page.

disagreements.positions: Agent 4 now cites Plus $115->$140 (+22%) and Advanced $275->$340 (+24%) from Aug 1, 2026 as verified against Intuit; round 1 relied on vendor blogs (13-70%).
disagreements.resolution: Partly verified. Intuit's pricing page lists Plus $140/mo, Advanced $340/mo, Essentials $85, Simple Start $38. Intuit's product-update page confirms that Essentials, Plus and Advanced change for renewals on or after Aug 1, 2026, with Simple Start unchanged, but it gives no dollar amounts, so the 'from' prices are not on an Intuit page. The increase is real and already inside the GBS +13-14% guide; churn risk is a watch item, not a number change.

disagreements.topic: Insider selling as a bear signal (agent 3)
disagreements.positions: Round 1: agent 3 cited CEO sales ($26.6M, Jan 2026). Round 2: agent 3 reports all executive 10b5-1 plans were terminated.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed by the 8-K of 2026-03-16: the founder and executive team terminated all outstanding 10b5-1 sale plans, and the company said it would substantially accelerate repurchases of up to $3.5B remaining at Jan 31, 2026 ($1.8B bought in 1H FY26, +40% y/y). The insider-selling point is dropped.

disagreements.topic: Exit multiple (12.5x vs 13.5x FY28 EPS) and FCF required yield (7.5-8.5%)
disagreements.positions: Agent 1 uses 13.5x and 8%; agents 2-5 use 12.5x; agent 4 uses 8.5% and agent 3 uses 7.5%.
disagreements.resolution: Not settleable by search; it is a judgment on the AI-disruption discount. 12.5x (about today's 11.6x forward plus modest normalization) and 8% are the reconciled values. Agent 1's higher P/E and agent 4's higher yield roughly offset in the mean.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' methods; FY27 guide $22.88-23.12 against a $268 price.

disagreements.topic: Timing of Q1 FY27 results (1-month window)
disagreements.positions: All five agents: late Nov or about Dec 1, outside the window.
disagreements.resolution: A search summary again points to Dec 1, 2026, but Intuit has not published a date release, and the Sep 17 Investor Day release reaffirmed Q1 guidance ($4.294-4.313B revenue, $2.44-2.48 EPS) without giving one. Either way it falls outside the window, so the 1-month ladder stays at the agents' mean.
disagreements.evidence: Intuit Investor Day press release, 2026-09-17; Alpha Vantage earnings calendar shows no date yet.

revision_check.agent_1: Took up the FCF normalization (leg $331->$310), the HRB floor (TB $190->$185) and higher accretion, but haircut accretion to 3.5% on a funding argument that double-counts SBC. FV $345->$328, still the highest, on a 13.5x multiple. Its only new source is my round-1 fact-check, so it added no independent evidence.
revision_check.agent_2: Accepted the share-loss reading, the SBC pre-tax/after-tax split and the FCF normalization. It added an in-lane HRB call source (industry growth to moderate in 2027; HRB held assisted share). FV $322->$316, bear 28% at $165. A good revision.
revision_check.agent_3: Raised FY28 EPS to $25.0, down-weighted the Goldman framework and tied its GAAP leg to its own numbers. It found the Mar 16 8-K (insider plans terminated) and the Stifel downgrade, which is real in-lane work. FV $298->$310; the only agent to move up.
revision_check.agent_4: Fixed the share count and FCF base (leg $357->$296) and replaced the vendor-blog price claims with Intuit's pricing (confirmed: Plus $140, Advanced $340). FV $336->$310. The FCF leg is now the lowest because it combines 10% growth with an 8.5% yield on only 255M shares.
revision_check.agent_5: Corrected HRB to 6.6x, cut FCF growth from 15% to 8% and fixed the guide date. It added an explicit 20% Chegg-type branch, which gives the fattest left tail (P(>=214) 0.71). FV $334->$315. Its new sources are mostly my round-1 citations.

one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company event before 2026-10-29 (Q1 FY27 results about Dec 1, unconfirmed; Investor Day already reaffirmed guidance), and the revised agents agree closely on a near-symmetric about 14% monthly spread around $268, so I use their round-2 mean unchanged.
confidence_reason: The one new fact I established (net SBC issuance about 1%/yr, so net accretion about 5% at current prices) is primary-sourced and pushes the center back up, but it is worth only about $5-8/share on fair value. The left-tail question is settled only by the Jan-Apr 2027 tax season. The round-2 convergence mostly reflects agents adopting round-1 findings rather than new independent evidence.
thesis_break_reason: About 8.5x FY27 guided SBC-inclusive EPS of $23 and about an 11% normalized SBC-burdened FCF yield. Below it the market would be pricing an earnings decline: a failed 2027 tax season (TurboTax units down again against a growing self-prepared category), a guide cut at Q2/Q3, or QuickBooks customer growth turning negative after the Aug 2026 price rises. The revised agents sit at $185-200 (mean $193). An HRB-like 6.6x on flat EPS (about $150-160) would confirm the break.
key_drivers: FY27 guide reaffirmed Sep 17: revenue +9-10% (TurboTax +2-3%, GBS +13-14%), non-GAAP EPS $22.88-23.12 including about $5.81 of SBC; $268 is about 11.6x.

Buybacks are more accretive than modeled: FY26 net employee issuance was only 2.6M shares against 13.4M repurchased (-3.8% count at about $409 average). At about $270, $5-6B a year retires about 5-6% net, supporting FY28 EPS of about $25.8.
FY26 OCF includes a one-off $1.28B OBBBA deferred-tax benefit (about $0.7B more in FY27); normalized SBC-burdened FCF is about $5.3B, or about a 7.5% yield.
TurboTax lost about 3.7 points of relative share in the 2026 season (units -2% vs IRS self-prepared e-file +1.7%), and the HRB comparable is at about 6.6x. The 2027 season decides the left tail.
QBO list prices rose on Aug 1, 2026 (Plus $140, Advanced $340): an ARPC tailwind with churn risk, with online paying customers up only 3% in FY26.

fair_value.reason: P/E leg: FY28 SBC-inclusive EPS about $25.8 (FY27 $23.0, revenue +8-9%, modest leverage, about 5% net share reduction at current prices) x 12.5x = about $322. FCF leg: normalized FY28 SBC-burdened FCF about $6.3B on about 250M average shares = about $25.2/share at 8% = about $315, less about $2/share net debt. Blend about $320, vs the revised agents' mean of $316 and my round-1 $318.

summary: Round 2 converged: fair values $310-328 (mean $316), P(>=$268 in a year) 0.535-0.575, thesis breaks $185-200. Almost all of that movement came from the agents adopting round-1 findings (normalized FCF, HRB at 6.6x, TurboTax share loss), not from new evidence. The one new primary fact is that buybacks are more accretive than anyone modeled: FY26 net employee issuance was only about 1% of shares, so $5-6B a year at about $270 cuts the count about 5% net. That lifts fair value to about $320 and the middle of the ladder by about a point. INTU is cheap at about 11.6x FY27 SBC-inclusive EPS, but the left tail stays fat until the Jan-Apr 2027 tax season shows whether TurboTax share loss continues.

sizing.overlap: None; the portfolio is all cash. Its drivers (AI disruption of application software, US consumer tax and SMB spending) would be shared with any future software or fintech holdings.
sizing.reason: Round 2 slightly firms the value case (heavier buyback accretion, insider sales halted, QBO pricing power), but the decisive evidence, the 2027 tax season, is 4-7 months away and realized volatility is about 50%. So the cap stays at 6%, built in tranches around the Q1 and Q2 prints. Liquidity is ample, and there is no lock-up or index event.
